title: Minimax ATE Estimation with Auxiliary Covariate-Only Registry Samples
banked_reason: Terminal D-0.5 proposal NO-PASS: bounded angles exhausted without an authorable field-level kernel; original all-budget matching remains unproved and was forecast subfield, not mathematically refuted.
gap_reasons: The full all-resource covariate-only R_X match is the explicitly retained unresolved branch of stat_reverseannotation_ate_frontier (especially oeq:outcome-mark-value), so this is a narrowing/retry rather than an independent repo-novel kernel.

No surviving seed supplied a structurally new strict X-only versus XY separation kernel. The artifact records a rejected feasibility core, not a completed proposal; finite-budget separation is not proved impossible.

The directed kernel fails the novelty and well-posedness check. Outcome-only calibration cannot distinguish the inherited interaction witnesses, even with exact treatment margins. Distinct observed laws cannot be exactly indistinguishable in the actual experiment because at least one complete record is observed. Joint covariance reconstruction recodes conditional contrasts; unrestricted minimality permits supplying the target itself. A substantive question requires an independently specified calibration family, observation experiment, and information order.
proof_attempt_summary: Attempted an explicit matched all-budget ATE squared-risk frontier for complete records plus covariate-only registries, then two distinct resource-separation and minimal-calibration pivots; all three angles ended without an authorable field-level kernel. No D0 derivation or Lean formalization occurred, and presolve polynomial and lower-family components remain unverified rather than delivered results. The original finite-budget matching question remains open; the independent validity gate found the repo-subsumption rationale overbroad but confirmed terminal NO-PASS under the field floor because the original gate forecast only subfield novelty and the pivots supplied no new kernel.
tldr: Covariate registries estimate the population weights in an identified average treatment effect without observing the treatment marks needed for confounding adjustment. The research target is an explicitly evaluated, universal-constant minimax squared-risk frontier for every complete-record budget, registry budget, and alphabet size over the published unrestricted discrete overlap model. Separate treatment and mass degrees, observable localization, and normalized moment priors provide the starting machinery. The full risk match and its exact consistency and label-limited phases are open. The existing benefit and saturated-consistency results are inherited.
gap: The available complete-record result, coarse known-marginal obstruction, regular two-sample efficiency theory, and failed reverse-annotation manuscript leave finite registry uncertainty unpriced in unrestricted signed-ATE squared risk. The maintained model is the observed-data class of Zeng et al., Section 2, at overlap one quarter; totalizing null-cell conditionals changes no observed law or target.
fill: An evaluated matched \(R_X(n,m,d)\) and total attaining procedure would price this interaction and identify when registry expansion reaches consistency or the \(n^{-1}\) label floor. Only this full point-risk frontier constitutes completion.
